origin.description: Generate R bootstrap replicates of a statistic applied to a time series. Replicates use fixed blocks, geometric blocks, a user model, or phase scrambling.
origin.usage: tsboot(tseries, statistic, R, l = NULL, sim = "model", endcorr = TRUE, n.sim = NROW(tseries), orig.t = TRUE, ran.gen, ran.args = NULL, norm = TRUE, ..., parallel = c("no", "multicore", "snow"), ncpus = getOption("boot.ncpus", 1L), cl = NULL)

arguments.name: tseries
arguments.text: A univariate or multivariate time series.

arguments.name: statistic
arguments.text: Function applied to each series. It receives a series of length n.sim and returns a vector. Further arguments are passed through ....

arguments.name: R
arguments.text: Positive integer, the number of bootstrap replicates.

arguments.name: sim
arguments.text: "model" for model-based resampling, "fixed" for blocks of length l, "geom" for geometric block lengths with mean l, or "scramble" for phase scrambling.

arguments.name: l
arguments.text: Fixed block length, or the mean of the geometric block lengths. A positive integer no longer than the series. Not used for "model" or "scramble".

arguments.name: endcorr
arguments.text: If true, block starts may fall anywhere in the series and blocks wrap. If false, starts are restricted so a block of length l stays inside the series. Forced to true for "geom".

arguments.name: n.sim
arguments.text: Length of each simulated series. Defaults to the number of observations.

arguments.name: orig.t
arguments.text: If true, t0 is statistic applied to the original series. If false, t0 is NULL.

arguments.name: ran.gen
arguments.text: Function of the series, n.sim, and ran.args. For "model" it builds the replicate. For the block methods it post-blackens the stitched blocks. The default returns the series unchanged.

arguments.name: ran.args
arguments.text: Extra object passed to ran.gen. NULL when ran.gen needs nothing beyond its three arguments.

arguments.name: norm
arguments.text: For phase scrambling, true uses normal margins and false restores the exact empirical margins.
Named arguments forwarded to statistic on every call.

arguments.name: parallel, ncpus, cl
arguments.text: Optional parallel backend. The comparison here is serial.

origin.details: Fixed blocks of length l are laid end to end until the replicate has length n.sim. Geometric blocks use the same stitching, with lengths drawn so their mean is l. Passing ran.gen post-blackens those replicates. Model-based replicates are produced entirely by ran.gen. Phase scrambling randomizes the Fourier phases of the centered series. The manual's lynx example fits an autoregression on each replicate; the example below is the same block bootstrap with the mean of a short series.
origin.value: An object of class "boot" with t0, t, R, data (the original series; the manual calls this component tseries), statistic, sim, and n.sim. Block methods also store l and endcorr. "model" stores ran.gen and ran.args. "scramble" stores norm. The attribute boot_type is "tsboot".
origin.example:
set.seed(1)
series <- 1:30
fixed <- tsboot(series, function(tsb) mean(tsb), R = 20, l = 5, sim = "fixed")
cat(sprintf("t0 %.10g\n", fixed$t0))
cat(sprintf("%.10g\n", fixed$t[, 1]), sep = "")
set.seed(1)
geom <- tsboot(series, function(tsb) mean(tsb), R = 20, l = 5, sim = "geom")
cat("geom\n")
cat(sprintf("t0 %.10g\n", geom$t0))
cat(sprintf("%.10g\n", geom$t[, 1]), sep = "")

translation.description: Generate R bootstrap replicates of a statistic applied to a time series. Replicates use fixed blocks, geometric blocks, a user model, or phase scrambling.
translation.usage: tsboot(tseries, statistic, R, l=None, sim="model", endcorr=True, n_sim=None, orig_t=True, ran_gen=None, ran_args=None, norm=True, parallel="no", ncpus=1, cl=None, **kwargs)

arguments.name: tseries
arguments.text: A one-dimensional series or a two-dimensional array with one row per time and one column per variable.

arguments.name: statistic
arguments.text: Function applied to each series. It receives a series of length n_sim and returns a vector. Further arguments are passed as keywords.

arguments.name: R
arguments.text: Positive number of bootstrap replicates. A non-integer is truncated toward zero with floor.

arguments.name: sim
arguments.text: "model" for model-based resampling, "fixed" for blocks of length l, "geom" for geometric block lengths with mean l, or "scramble" for phase scrambling.

arguments.name: l
arguments.text: Fixed block length, or the mean of the geometric block lengths. A positive number no longer than the series. Not used for "model" or "scramble".

arguments.name: endcorr
arguments.text: If true, block starts may fall anywhere in the series and blocks wrap. If false, starts are restricted so a block of length l stays inside the series. Forced to true for "geom".

arguments.name: n_sim
arguments.text: Length of each simulated series. The default is the number of observations.

arguments.name: orig_t
arguments.text: If true, t0 is statistic applied to the original series. If false, t0 is None.

arguments.name: ran_gen
arguments.text: Function of the series, n_sim, and ran_args. For "model" it builds the replicate. For the block methods it post-blackens the stitched blocks. The default returns the series unchanged.

arguments.name: ran_args
arguments.text: Extra object passed to ran_gen. None when ran_gen needs nothing beyond its three arguments.

arguments.name: norm
arguments.text: For phase scrambling, true uses normal margins and false restores the exact empirical margins.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Keyword arguments forwarded to statistic on every call.

arguments.name: parallel, ncpus, cl
arguments.text: Accepted for the R signature. Only serial evaluation is implemented; parallel="no" is the default.

translation.details: Fixed blocks of length l are laid end to end until the replicate has length n_sim. Geometric blocks use the same stitching. Lengths are 1 plus an R geometric draw, which is a Poisson of an exponential, and a normal draw on that path is qnorm of two uniforms packed the way R's Inversion generator packs them. Passing ran_gen post-blackens block replicates. Model-based replicates are produced entirely by ran_gen. Phase scrambling randomizes the Fourier phases of the centered series. Random integers come from boot.rng sample_int, matching R sample.int. The manual's lynx example fits an autoregression on each replicate; the example below is the same block bootstrap with the mean of a short series.
translation.value: A Tsboot object with t0, t, R, data (the original series), statistic, sim, and n_sim. Block methods also store l and endcorr. "model" stores ran_gen and ran_args. "scramble" stores norm. boot_type is "tsboot". t has one row per replicate.
translation.example:
from boot.rng import set_seed
from boot.series import tsboot
import numpy as np

set_seed(1)
series = list(range(1, 31))
fixed = tsboot(series, lambda tsb: float(np.mean(tsb)), R=20, l=5, sim="fixed")
print(f"t0 {fixed.t0:.10g}")
for value in fixed.t[:, 0]:
    print(f"{value:.10g}")
set_seed(1)
geom = tsboot(series, lambda tsb: float(np.mean(tsb)), R=20, l=5, sim="geom")
print("geom")
print(f"t0 {geom.t0:.10g}")
for value in geom.t[:, 0]:
    print(f"{value:.10g}")
